batch_note: Yes. The 16 textual items (A/B/C/D 01-05) are all one template: a 2x2-plus-confound design of named sites, where the key is the single comparison varying only the hypothesis's factor in the predicted direction (or, for weaken, the rival-only site beating the hypothesis-only site). The three distractors are always drawn from the same menu: a reversed comparison, the comparison that isolates the rival factor, and a comparison carrying the shared confound (slope, elevation, rail, fault, slump year, wet summers, market town). A student who has seen two of these can solve the rest by tagging sites and striking the reversed, rival-only and confounded options, without engaging the specific science or history. The 'weaken' items additionally lean repeatedly on the 'rival-only beats hypothesis-only' move. The 16 table items are likewise one template: a two-condition threshold filter (ratio or difference plus a categorical gate), with the option text printing only some of the needed cells, one near-miss failing each condition, and one 'biggest/most extreme' lure. Keys do not track letter position, but the structural recipe is predictable across items.
